**Kentucky Sales Tax Quick Facts**


**Kentucky sales tax rate:**


6%


**Local taxes:**


No


**Economic nexus threshold:**


$100,000 in gross sales to customers in the state in the previous or current calendar year


**What sales count toward the threshold:**


Gross sales including marketplace sales


**Tax authority:**


[Kentucky Department of Revenue](https://revenue.ky.gov/Pages/index.aspx)


**Tax portal:**


[Kentucky Taxpayer Portal](https://mytaxes.ky.gov/rptp/portal/home/!ut/p/z1/04_Sj9CPykssy0xPLMnMz0vMAfIjo8zijS0MnN09DIy83EODjQwc_R1DTcIcvYAsE_1wQgqigNIGOICjAVB_FCElXvpR6Tn5SRDXOOYlGVuk60cVpaalFqUW6ZUWAYUzSkoKiq1UDVQNysvL9dLz89NzUvWS83NVDbBpycgvLtGPQFWpX5AbYaAblVRZ7qioCACcsljT/dz/d5/L2dBISEvZ0FBIS9nQSEh/)


**SaaS taxable:**


Yes


**Administration difficulty:**

Kentucky’s sales tax rate is a flat 6% with no local added taxes. It’s the same whether you’re selling in Louisville, Lexington or Bowling Green. This makes Kentucky one of the easier states in which to operate.


That said, the state taxes[SaaS](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/sales-tax-software) , digital goods, and a wide range of services, so you’ll want to ensure you’re charging sales tax correctly on your products.


This guide walks you through what's taxable in Kentucky, when you need to register, how to calculate what you owe, and how to file and pay the Kentucky Department of Revenue on time.


## Kentucky Sales Tax at a Glance


Kentucky charges a flat 6% sales tax rate statewide. There are no local, county, or city add-ons anywhere in the state.


Kentucky sales tax applies to retail sales and leases of tangible personal property, digital property, and a long list of specified services. The Kentucky Department of Revenue's Division of Sales and Use Tax administers the tax, and businesses handle registration, filing, and payment through the[Kentucky Taxpayer Portal](http://mytaxes.ky.gov/) .


## Taxable Categories: What Kentucky Sales Tax Applies To


### SaaS and Digital Products


SaaS is taxable in Kentucky. The state classifies remotely accessed software, sometimes called “prewritten computer software access services,” as taxable digital property. This applies whether your customer is a business buying a subscription for internal use or a consumer paying for a personal account.


Kentucky also taxes specified digital products, including digital audio works, digital audio-visual works, and e-books, when they're delivered electronically to a customer. If you sell subscriptions, downloads, or cloud-based tools to Kentucky customers, you're very likely required to collect sales tax on those transactions.


[Sphere](https://www.getsphere.com/) classifies your Kentucky transactions automatically, so you don't have to manually track which of your products count as digital property under state law.


### Tangible Personal Property (TPP)


Physical goods sold in Kentucky are taxed at the standard 6% rate. Alcohol is also taxable at 6%, a change that took effect back in April 2009.


Kentucky exempts most unprepared groceries and unprocessed foods from sales tax, along with prescription drugs and certain medical equipment. However, there are exceptions and candy, soft drinks, and hot or prepared foods are taxable even though they're sold alongside exempt grocery items.


### Taxable Services


Kentucky taxes a broader range of services than most of the country, covering roughly 75 enumerated categories under Kentucky law.


Taxable services include but are not limited to:


- Landscaping and lawn care
- Photography
- Fitness memberships & personal training
- Janitorial services
- Veterinary services for small animals
- Dry cleaning and laundry services
- Marketing
- Telemarketing
- Lobbying
- Website design and hosting
- Parking services
- Data brokerage services (effective August 1, 2026)


Learn more about[sales tax on services in Kentucky here](https://taxanswers.ky.gov/Sales-and-Excise-Taxes/Pages/default.aspx) .


Many of these services became taxable in 2018 when the state expanded their tax base. Because of that, the state provides relief for small scale sellers whose offerings became newly taxable at the time. If you sell one or more of these services and your gross receipts stay under $12,000 in a calendar year, you're not required to maintain an active sales tax permit for that year. However, if you cross that threshold your sales from then on become taxable.


## Monitoring: When Kentucky Sales Tax Applies to You


Businesses with physical presence in Kentucky or who surpass a certain amount of sales in Kentucky are required to collect sales tax from buyers in the state.


### Economic Nexus Threshold


Kentucky's economic nexus threshold is $100,000 in gross receipts from Kentucky sales during the current or previous calendar year. Both taxable and exempt sales count toward that $100,000 figure. Exempt services, however, are not included in the calculation. If your business does more than $100,000 in gross receipts in the state, no matter where you are located, you’re required to register for and collect Kentucky sales tax.


[Sphere](https://www.getsphere.com/) monitors your Kentucky gross receipts across all your sales channels and alerts you before you approach the threshold, so registration never catches you off guard.


### Physical Nexus


Any physical presence in Kentucky creates[sales tax nexus](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/nexus-tax-software) regardless of your revenue. That includes an office, a warehouse, inventory stored in a Kentucky fulfillment center, or an employee or contractor working in the state. Unlike economic nexus, Physical presence triggers a registration requirement from your first transaction.


### Marketplace Facilitators


Marketplace facilitators like Amazon, Etsy, and Walmart who handle payments for 3rd party sellers are required to collect and remit Kentucky sales tax on behalf of the retailers who sell through their platforms. However, keep in mind that if you also sell directly through your own website or store, those direct sales remain your responsibility to tax and remit even after you register.


## Registration: How to Register for Kentucky Sales Tax


### How to Register


Register for your Kentucky sales tax permit at the[KY Taxpayer Portal](http://mytaxes.ky.gov/) .


Click "Register a New Account" and work through the application. Processing isn't instant. Kentucky mails a PIN to your business address, and you need that PIN to activate full access to the portal.


This process applies to both in-state and remote sellers.


### Registration Fees


There's no fee to register for a Kentucky sales tax account.


[Sphere](https://www.getsphere.com/) manages the entire KY Taxpayer Portal registration process for you, including handling the PIN activation step, so your team doesn't have to track down a piece of physical mail before you can start collecting tax.


## Calculation: Kentucky Sales Tax Rates


### State Rate


Kentucky's sales tax rate is a flat 6% on all taxable transactions statewide. Because there's no local rate layered on top, you don't need to look up a local sales tax rate for every order. A sale to a customer in Louisville is taxed at the exact same rate as a sale to a customer in Bowling Green or a small rural county.


### What the Rate Applies To


The 6% rate applies to taxable tangible personal property, SaaS, specified digital products, and the enumerated taxable services covered above. It doesn't apply to groceries, prescription drugs, or any service that isn't specifically listed as taxable under Kentucky law. Shipping charges generally follow the taxability of the item being shipped, so shipping on a taxable sale is typically taxable, too.


Keep in mind that sales tax is separate from Kentucky's excise taxes, which apply to specific categories like motor vehicle rentals and ride-sharing services rather than general retail sales. A transaction can be subject to an excise tax, sales tax, or both, depending on what you're selling.


## Filing: How and When to File Kentucky Sales Tax Returns


### Filing via KY Taxpayer Portal


File Kentucky sales tax returns electronically through the KY Taxpayer Portal. If you're registered but had no taxable sales during a given period, you still need to file a zero return. Skipping a zero return can still trigger penalties, so don't assume no sales means no filing obligation.


### Filing Deadlines


Most filers owe their sales and use tax return on the 20th day of the month following the reporting period. If the 20th falls on a weekend or a holiday, the deadline typically moves to the next business day. Annual filers have their return due by January 20 of the following year.


### Filing Frequency Thresholds


The Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns your filing frequency, monthly, quarterly, or annual, based on your prior-year tax liability, and it reviews and adjusts frequencies each June.


If your business circumstances change significantly, you can request a frequency change directly from the department rather than waiting for the annual review.


### Late Filing Penalties


Kentucky adds a 25% Cost of Collection Fee to any unpaid tax that's still outstanding 60 days after the Original Notice Date. On top of that, interest accrues on unpaid tax from the original due date, and the rate is set at 9% per year effective January 1, 2026. Interest can't be waived, even if a penalty is.


Also note that you're liable for uncollected tax whether or not you registered on time. Failing to register or collect sales tax doesn't stop the liability from building. If you think you may have missed your registration date in Kentucky and owe back taxes, consider looking into your options for remediation before the state finds you first.


## Remittance: How to Pay Kentucky Sales Tax


Remit Kentucky sales tax via ACH debit at the same time as you file with the KY Taxpayer Portal.
